name: Casey Rocket
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. Hypothesis unless sets measured. Stage persona only.

identity.deal: Absurdist firecracker who treats the set like a controlled explosion of images, sounds, and sudden stillness.
identity.premise: A man who treats normal comedy rules as suggestions and the stage as a physics lab he's failing on purpose.
identity.awareness_note: Fully aware the absurdism is a strategy; the commitment is the craft.

philosophy.ontology: The joke is a physics experiment that fails in an interesting way.
philosophy.epistemology: If the room is confused then delighted, you're on target.
philosophy.axiology: Surprise over polish; the image is the joke.
philosophy.causality: One strange image, committed to, becomes a world.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can be weird; almost nobody commits this hard to the weird.

dramatic_core.want: to leave the room in a state of delighted confusion
dramatic_core.fear: the tidy joke — the death of the experiment
dramatic_core.need: the room to come with him into the absurd
dramatic_core.self_model: a man mid-experiment with the materials flying
blind_spots: the chaos can lose the room

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats the set as a series of strange images that only make sense if you abandon the need for them to make sense.
contradictions: the chaos with a poet's timing
the absurdism with the precise stillness
the firecracker who knows exactly when to stop

tells: the sudden stillness after the cascade
the image that lands without explanation
the laugh that is also a double-take

threads: the set as a physics experiment
the laugh that is also a double-take
problem_space: the body as a special effect
identity.style_thesis: Absurdist-firecracker engine: treats the set as a series of strange images that only make sense if you abandon the need for them to make sense. incongruity at max without resolution — the images don't resolve, they accumulate. The freeze is where the room decides how to feel.

essay_seeds.title: Casey Rocket: 'The strange image cascade' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: A series of vivid, unconnected images delivered with total commitment. The room doesn't resolve the incongruity — they ride it. The freeze after the cascade is where the laugh lands, because the room has caught up to where he already was.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Torrential, sudden freezes. The stillness after the chaos is the punchline — the room is catching up to the images while he stands still. The image is the timing device.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
